source_identity: Purdue GIS FID 776, BUILDING_N Sigma Pi, BLDG_ABBR SOSP; owner GREEK, address 130 Russell St. Official Sigma Pi page independently confirms the Purdue Chapter House at 130 N. Russell St.
source_date: GIS and county assessor records retrieved 2026-10-26; state imagery coverage 2022-2025; 2018 QL2 LiDAR; Eta Data November 2004 chapter-house photographs; Purdue Debris 1932 historical illustration.
source_crs_and_transform: EPSG:4326; Purdue project local approximate-meter conversion as written in modular/AGENTS.md. Asset retained campus coordinates because it remains a simple massing library.

position.method: Projected all 37 GIS outer-ring vertices into Purdue campus coordinates and built the shell from those vertices. Independently transformed the source ring to the state imagery service's native EPSG:3857 and overlaid it on current Indiana orthophotography; the boundary tracks the visible roof outline closely.
position.limitation: Current orthophotography corroborates roof-plan registration; the hidden structural wall line relative to the roof overhang is not visible or measured.

plan_geometry.method: Exact vertex-preserving reconstruction of the single official FID 776 ring in project local approximate meters; per-vertex nearest error checked after fresh reopen.
plan_geometry.discrepancy: The layer metadata reports EPSG:3857 (latestWkid 3857), and direct projection of the delivered EPSG:4326 ring gives 817.385769 m2 / 154.003222677 m, matching the stored Shape__Area/Shape__Length within rounding (817.39453125 / 154.003222658). These are planar Web Mercator values; WGS84 geodesic ground-surface values are 473.159331 m2 / 117.119700 m. Current orthophoto supports the ring as roof perimeter only; the structural wall line is unverified.

vertical_geometry.evidence: 2018 QL2 tile in2018_29951885_12.copc.laz overlaps the exact FID 776 ring. Nearby class-2 ground median is 622.83 ft NAVD88. Class-1 returns >=650 ft (a transparent analysis filter, not a semantic roof class) have p10=654.792, median=661.415, p90=663.02, max=665.36 ft NAVD88, equivalent to about 9.74-12.25 m above the ground median at p10-p90 and 12.96 m at max. After clipping candidate source heights to the 5th-95th percentile range and interpolating a 0.9 m constrained mesh, the asset roof surface ranges 9.45-12.36 m above the local ground datum; depressed edges and central high bands support roof articulation. Dated November 2004 house photos support broad facade and roof-form cues after the 1989 addition, but do not measure vertical dimensions.
vertical_geometry.uncertainty: No class-6 building returns were present. Class-1 returns are unclassified; vegetation or other surface points may remain. The source supports roof-surface heights/articulation but does not establish the wall line, occupied story count, or surveyed roof structure. Wall height (9.35 m), window arrangement, and entry dimensions remain estimates.

geometry_changes: Replaced generic 16-vertex massing shell (16.0 m tall) with the exact 37-vertex FID 776 GIS outer ring; the original bounds were already within about 0.3 m of the projected ring.

Changed the unsupported 16.0 m shell to an estimated 9.35 m wall height, set just below the robust LiDAR-derived roof surface so the simplified wall volume meets the roof skin; wall height and story count remain estimates.
Applied restrained stucco and exterior wood-trim material cues grounded in the 2004 chapter newsletter.

Corrected the area/perimeter interpretation: GIS Shape__Area/Length are EPSG:3857 planar metrics and reconcile with the source ring after projection; geodesic metrics are reported separately. Added the 1932 Sigma Pi page as historical visual evidence with explicit pre-1989 limits and stored these source/uncertainty notes as Blender custom properties.

Replaced the flat roof cap with a constrained 0.9 m mesh clipped to the exact GIS ring and interpolated from 1,094 2018 QL2 class-1 returns at or above the documented 650 ft analysis threshold. Source heights are clipped to their 5th-95th percentile range to reduce isolated-return influence; vegetation and classification limits are recorded.

Updated the street-facing facade with masonry at the lower level, Tudor half-timber cues above, multiple window tiers, and a street entry based on the November 2004 Eta Data house photographs; architectural dimensions remain unknown, so these remain qualitative cues.
Kept the 9.35 m wall shell, window count, and entry dimensions explicitly estimated; LiDAR constrains roof surface only and does not resolve wall height or floor count.

Replaced the sparse single-segment trim with a readable Tudor half-timber pattern across three east-facing GIS facade runs, including vertical stiles, horizontal rails, crossed braces, and divided window casings. November 2004 Eta Data photographs on pp. 1 and 6 support these qualitative cues; exact layout and dimensions remain schematic.

unresolved: The November 2004 house photos provide dated-in-context visual evidence after the 1989 addition, but no measured elevation or exact opening schedule; facade spacing and all architectural dimensions remain schematic.

No measured current wall line or floor count; shell height and structural wall registration remain estimated. 2018 LiDAR returns are unclassified, so vegetation and interpolation uncertainty remain in the roof surface.
The 2018 LiDAR-derived footprint differs materially from the Purdue GIS ring and is not substituted for FID 776.
Master integration remains pending; contributors do not own the master blend.

validation.note: A fresh Blender 5.2.3 LTS background process opened the saved .blend read-only and ran audit/sigma_pi/reopen_validation.py.
